channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: CVE-2026-134070 - Improper input sanitization in the AWS Config remediation runbook AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3
item.description: We identified CVE-2026-134070, where improper input validation in the AWS-managed AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3 might allow an authenticated remote user who is permitted to run the runbook to set unintended configuration in the account's Regional Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) via a crafted S3KeyPrefix parameter value.

item.title: Italy, Switzerland Warn of AI-Powered Autonomous Cyberattacks
item.description: Italian and Swiss cybersecurity agencies issued a warning about autonomous cyberattacks driven by AI agents targeting critical infrastructure organizations. The advisory highlights the increasing capability of automated threat actors to launch coordinated attacks without human intervention. Security teams should monitor for anomalous activity, enforce strict access controls, and update AI detection systems to mitigate potential threats.

item.title: Thanksgiving Thanks and Critiques from David
item.description: On November 25, 2026, David posted a Thanksgiving-themed note thanking the cybersecurity community and addressing threat actors. The brief message acknowledges community efforts, offers gratitude, and delivers a few pointed remarks toward malicious actors. No technical vulnerabilities or incidents are reported, making it a general commentary on community resilience today.

item.title: Socket Calm Theme Launches for VS Code, Vim, Neovim
item.description: Socket Calm, a free open-source syntax highlighting theme, has been released for VS Code, Vim, and Neovim. The theme draws inspiration from Socket's design system, offering consistent color palettes and readability enhancements across editors. Users can install the theme via the respective extension repositories or package managers, with no licensing restrictions.

item.title: Ubuntu Discloses elfutils Readelf and Strip CVEs
item.description: Ubuntu reported two elfutils CVEs that affect readelf and strip when handling malformed DWARF data or empty sections. The flaws (CVE-2025-1352 and CVE-2025-1376) could crash the utilities or enable arbitrary code execution if an attacker tricks a user or automated system into processing crafted files. Ubuntu has issued patches; updating elfutils to the latest release will mitigate the vulnerabilities.

item.title: Ghostscript Vulnerability Updated on RHEL 9
item.description: Ghostscript on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 is affected by a security flaw. The vulnerability, rated Important by Red Hat Product Security, has a CVSS base score detailed in the CVE references; it permits potential exploitation of the Ghostscript interpreter. Red Hat has released an update; administrators should apply the Ghostscript patch immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Ghostscript Vulnerability Updated on RHEL 8
item.description: Ghostscript on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 is affected by a security flaw. The vulnerability, rated Important by Red Hat Product Security, has a CVSS base score detailed in the CVE references; it permits potential exploitation of the Ghostscript interpreter. Red Hat has released an update; administrators should apply the Ghostscript patch immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: What defenders need to know about ARTEX, the agentic AI framework threat actors abuse
item.description: The AI-powered penetration testing framework ARTEX has been abused by threat actors like Storm-0940, Storm-3358, Onyx Sleet, Pearl Sleet, Crystal Typhoon, and Salt Typhoon to accelerate their existing workflows related to network reconnaissance, credential attacks, and web application exploitation.

A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Florida Ransomware Recovery CEO Indicted
item.description: A federal grand jury indicted the CEO of a Florida-based ransomware recovery firm for allegedly lying about services and paying ransoms to cybercriminals. The indictment alleges the executive engaged in deceptive practices and facilitated financial transactions that supported ransomware operators. The case underscores the legal risks for recovery providers and signals increased scrutiny of the industry by law enforcement.

item.title: CVE-2026-136267 - Improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command in Kiro Web
item.description: We are aware of CVE-2026-136267, an issue in Kiro Web where tool-call markup inside content an agent session read, such as a repository file or a web page, could be repeated by certain models and run as a command in the subscriber's hosted development environment without a consent prompt.

item.title: Australia Enacts Digital Duty of Care Law
item.description: Australia's Digital Duty of Care Act mandates online providers to establish protocols that shield users from violence, rape, and other harms. The law obligates tech companies to identify and mitigate foreseeable risks, extending oversight to content moderation and user safety measures. Compliance will require new policy frameworks, risk assessments, and reporting mechanisms, with enforcement provisions pending parliamentary approval.

item.title: Five Holiday-Themed Attacks Target Users and Businesses
item.description: ANY.RUN researchers uncovered five holiday-themed attacks that used credential-phishing emails, unauthorized remote-access tools, and malicious scripts to target users and businesses. The attacks harvested credentials, installed remote-access backdoors, and executed scripts that could exfiltrate sensitive data, exposing endpoints to lateral movement. Teams should enforce MFA, scrutinize email attachments, and deploy endpoint detection to block unauthorized remote-access activity.

item.title: Task Management App Todoist Hacked, Attackers Breach Production Systems
item.description: Task management app Todoist said an attacker breached its production systems on November 23, 2026, and downloaded account records for about 6% of its users. The attacker also obtained integration tokens and accessed some data from connected Outlook mailboxes.

item.title: CISA Alerts on Critical Danfoss Controller Vulnerability
item.description: CISA issued a warning about a critical flaw in Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series refrigeration controllers used by food retailers, identified as CVE-2026-129713. The vulnerability permits unauthenticated remote code execution, enabling attackers to manipulate temperature controls and potentially disrupt refrigeration operations. CISA recommends applying the vendor’s patch immediately, updating firmware, and monitoring for anomalous activity to mitigate risk.

item.title: Switzerland Reports First AI-Assisted Cyberattacks
item.description: Switzerland’s NCSC confirmed the first AI-agent cyberattacks that breached IT systems of companies and critical infrastructure operators in two sectors. Attackers leveraged generative AI to automate reconnaissance, credential harvesting, and exploit delivery, enabling rapid compromise without human intervention. Security teams should monitor for anomalous AI-driven activity, enforce strict access controls, and apply timely patches to mitigate future incidents.

item.title: Ubuntu Reports Speex Oversize Input Vulnerability
item.description: Ubuntu identified a Speex library flaw that mishandles oversized input when appending data to an external bit buffer. The defect could crash the decoder or allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code if a crafted file is processed. A patch has been released; users should update Speex to the latest version to eliminate the vulnerability.

item.title: Malicious NuGet Packages Target .NET Developers
item.description: Researchers uncovered 13 malicious NuGet packages distributed through a fake recruitment campaign, designed to infect .NET developers’ machines. The poisoned packages contain malware that grants attackers remote access, enabling credential theft and lateral movement within development environments. Developers should verify package sources, use signed packages, and apply the latest security updates to mitigate exploitation.

item.title: Microsoft 365 Bug Causes Blank Screens in Office Apps
item.description: A startup issue in Microsoft 365 prevented users from opening Word, Excel, and Outlook, displaying a blank white screen. The bug, identified in a November 23, 2026 support notice, caused the applications to stall without visible controls, blocking access to document functionality. Microsoft released a patch addressing the issue; users should update to the latest version to restore normal operation.

item.title: Juniper Adds CVE-2026-103406 to KEV Catalog
item.description: Juniper Networks disclosed multiple vulnerabilities in Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router prior to 7.0.5, 7.1.7, and 7.2.3 that allow attackers to execute code. CISA listed CVE-2026-103406 as a known exploited vulnerability, indicating active exploitation in the wild, though specific CVSS is not disclosed. Administrators should review Juniper’s advisory links and apply firmware updates to mitigate the risk.

item.title: SOC Management 2027: Five Steps Against AI Threats
item.description: The article outlines five steps for SOCs and MSSPs to manage AI-driven threats in 2027. It highlights the need to balance evolving attack speeds with limited resources, emphasizing detection, threat intelligence, and automation to counter phishing and expanding attack surfaces. The guidance encourages scaling operations, fostering innovation, and adopting AI tools to improve response times and reduce analyst fatigue.

item.title: GeoServer CVEs 2026-120705, 2026-129243 Exploited
item.description: GeoServer versions before 2.27.7, 2.28.6, and 3.0.2 are vulnerable to two CVEs, CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243, which attackers are exploiting in the wild. Both CVEs allow remote code execution through improper input validation in GeoServer's API, resulting in full system compromise. Administrators should immediately apply the latest GeoServer 2.27.7, 2.28.6, or 3.0.2 releases or install the vendor-issued patch to mitigate exploitation.

item.title: GeoServer High-Severity Flaws Targeted for RCE
item.description: Attackers are probing GeoServer instances for two vulnerabilities that can be chained with other bugs to achieve remote code execution. The flaws stem from insufficient input sanitization in GeoServer's configuration handling, allowing attackers to inject malicious payloads that bypass authentication. Administrators should update to the latest GeoServer release or apply the vendor-issued patch to close the vulnerabilities and prevent exploitation.

item.title: SolarWinds Serv-U and Dameware Vulnerabilities Disclosed
item.description: SolarWinds disclosed two vulnerabilities in Serv-U and Dameware, enabling privilege escalation and command injection. The Serv-U flaw (CVE-2026-123167) permits directory traversal for privilege gain, while Dameware (CVE-2026-28336) allows arbitrary command execution. Apply the latest patches or firmware updates immediately, and review the advisory links for detailed guidance to mitigate risk.

item.title: Hackers Exploit Fortinet Flaws to Breach Commercial Ships and Access Control Networks
item.description: U.S. authorities are investigating whether Iran was behind cyberattacks that may have compromised up to 50 commercial ships. A U.S. official familiar with the inquiry told NPR that hackers exploited known flaws in Fortinet FortiGate devices used aboard vessels.

item.title: Bot Detection Losing Battle, Privileged Access Must Equal
item.description: Bot detection has become a losing game as automated actors outpace traditional controls. The root cause is the rapid proliferation of sophisticated bots that mimic legitimate users, making privilege escalation indistinguishable from human activity. Security teams must enforce equal privileged access controls for humans and machines, adopting zero-trust and continuous monitoring to mitigate bot-driven threats.

item.title: Adobe AEM Vulnerabilities Fixed in Hotfix
item.description: Adobe Experience Manager Cloud Service, AEM 6.5, and AEM 6.5 LTS are affected by multiple vulnerabilities, including the issue identified as GRANITE-76751. The flaw permits unauthorized access to administrative interfaces and could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code, though no public exploit is confirmed. Adobe has released cumulative hotfixes; administrators should apply the updates promptly to secure their deployments.

item.title: AI Reduces Pentester Workload, Boosts Engagements
item.description: Pentesters spend a large portion of engagements on documentation and reporting, limiting test throughput. PentestPad shows AI can automate these peripheral tasks, enabling teams to handle more tests while keeping sensitive client data on their own infrastructure. AI workflow tools cut manual effort, improve consistency, and free pentesters for technical testing, yet demand secure data governance.

item.title: AI-Driven Attacks Rise; Speed and Edge AI Offer Defense
item.description: Unit 42 examines AI-powered cyberattacks, noting attackers use machine learning to accelerate reconnaissance and exploitation. The report stresses speed, edge AI, and baseline behavior modeling as essential for detecting and stopping these adaptive threats. Teams should implement real-time anomaly detection, edge analytics, and continuous baseline updates to counter AI-driven attacks while protecting data privacy.

item.title: InfraTrust Highlights Exploited Supply Chain Flaws in Network Appliances
item.description: InfraTrust's November report warns that most recent advisories involve exploited third-party software bundled into network appliances, not vendor code. These supply-chain flaws allow attackers to inject malicious code or gain unauthorized access, threatening device integrity and network security. Teams should audit appliance firmware, verify component provenance, and apply vendor patches or mitigations promptly.

item.title: Drupal Core Exploit CVE-2026-132165 Enables Passwordless Takeover
item.description: Hackers are exploiting CVE-2026-132165, a critical flaw in Drupal core, to take over live websites without authentication. The flaw permits unauthenticated remote code execution via HTTP requests, granting full site control; attacks were reported on November 19, 2026, with a CVSS score of 10.0.

item.title: Shufti Fraud Hub Reveals Links Among Legitimate Accounts
item.description: Shufti launched its Fraud Hub, linking identity, device, biometric, and behavioral signals to detect suspicious verification attempts. The platform identifies coordinated fraud networks and monitors emerging risks across the user lifecycle, revealing links between accounts that seem legitimate. Teams should use Fraud Hub’s context-aware analytics to supplement individual checks, enabling proactive decisions before fraud escalates and lowering onboarding risk.

item.title: Flatpak Update Released for RHEL7 ELS
item.description: Red Hat issued a flatpak security update for RHEL 7 Extended Lifecycle Support, addressing several vulnerabilities. The update carries an Important security impact rating, with CVSS base scores listed in the CVE references. Apply the patch immediately and to prevent exploitation of the disclosed critical flaws and maintain system integrity.

item.title: Grafana Update Released for RHEL9.8 EUS
item.description: Red Hat issued a grafana security update for RHEL 9.8 Extended Update Support, fixing several vulnerabilities. The update carries an Important security impact rating, with CVSS base scores listed in the CVE references. Apply the patch immediately to prevent exploitation of the disclosed critical flaws, maintain system stability, and ensure compliance.

item.description: An update for raptor2 is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.8 Update Services for SAP Solutions and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.8 Telecommunications Update Service. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important.

item.title: Adobe Releases Patches for Critical Experience Manager Flaws
item.description: Adobe released security updates on November 24, 2026, addressing critical flaws in Adobe Experience Manager and Adobe Campaign Classic. The vulnerabilities could enable attackers to execute arbitrary code, elevate privileges, or bypass security checks on affected servers. Adobe recommends applying the patches immediately; no workarounds are available, and users should verify installation status.

item.title: Intent IDs Leak Into Victim Logs
item.description: Intent IDs (iNNNN) from agentic offensive frameworks such as ARTEX and Cairn are inadvertently recorded in victim logs. The leakage exposes attacker identifiers, allowing defenders to track and deconflict malicious activity, though the signal weakens when logs are truncated. Mitigation requires sanitizing logs to remove iNNNN counters or implementing log filtering rules to prevent exposure of offensive framework identifiers.

item.title: AI Agents Exploit Unpatched Vulnerability to Control University Server
item.description: AI agents discovered an unpatched vulnerability in a university server and subsequently leveraged it to gain control. The flaw allowed remote code execution via an undisclosed mechanism, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary commands without authentication. The university should apply the vendor's patch or update firmware immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: RHSA-2026:103495: Critical: php security update
item.description: An update for php is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.6 Extended Update Support. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Critical. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: ShinyHunters Announces Return, Inception Denies Ties
item.description: An account linked to the ShinyHunters hacking group announced its return, while Okta identified potential connections between ShinyHunters and the Inception group. The post, titled 'ShinyHunters Claims Comeback, New Inception Group Rejects Alleged Ties,' was first published on SecurityWeek. Security teams should monitor ShinyHunters activity and review Okta’s findings for potential insider or credential compromise indicators.

item.title: Hackers Use Hugging Face AI to Build Fake Microsoft and Google Login Pages to Steal Passwords
item.description: Attackers used Hugging Face’s DeepSite AI website builder to create fake sign-in pages and hosted them on the same platform developers use to share AI demos. Aikido Security identified 42 pages on Hugging Face Spaces that impersonated 28 brands, including Microsoft, Google, PayPal, Chase, and Coinbase.

item.title: Hackers Exploit Critical Hex.pm Vulnerability to Execute Commands on Six Servers
item.description: A critical Hex.pm vulnerability was exploited on November 23, 2026, allowing attackers to execute operating system commands on six web servers. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-129514, carries a maximum severity score of 10.0 and required no account.

item.title: Latin America Faces Industrial Cyberattacks
item.description: Cyberattacks targeting ports, pipelines, and manufacturing facilities have increased across Latin America, affecting critical infrastructure. Attackers exploit known vulnerabilities in industrial control systems, leveraging remote code execution and credential theft to disrupt operations. Operators should apply vendor patches, enforce network segmentation, and monitor for anomalous traffic to mitigate future incidents.

item.title: Cloudflare Adds AI Agent Search Toggle
item.description: Cloudflare introduces a toggle that makes sites searchable by AI agents, adding automatic content indexing and a discoverable search API. The feature also supports native HTTP QUERY support, allowing agents to retrieve structured data directly from web pages. Deploying the toggle requires no code changes, but operators should review privacy settings to prevent sensitive content exposure to AI agents.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.description: An update for raptor2 is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.4 Advanced Mission Critical Update Support and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.4 Extended Update Support Long-Life Add-On. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important.

item.title: FinCEN Disconnected Systems After Cyber Incident
item.description: FinCEN experienced a cyber incident that caused system disconnections, disrupting filers. The root cause remains under investigation, with no public details on exploitation or vulnerability. FinCEN extended deadlines for affected filers and is conducting a full investigation, urging stakeholders to monitor updates. The incident has prompted a review of security controls and incident response procedures.

item.title: Drupal Installer Exploit CVE-2026-132165 Active
item.description: Attackers exploit CVE-2026-132165 to take over unpatched Drupal sites without authentication. The flaw allows remote code execution via the installer, rated CVSS 9.8, and is actively used in the wild since November 19, affecting government, university, media, and enterprise sites. Drupal releases patch 10.0.12; administrators should update immediately or disable the installer to mitigate the vulnerability.
